lede: Tuesday's Town Council meeting is the one to watch this week — the newly seated Council takes up second reading of the Colorado Wildfire Resiliency Code, a Land Use Code amendment that would change historic review and landscaping standards across town to meet state wildfire requirements, and that's a vote worth knowing about. Also on Tuesday, the Telluride Housing Authority is hashing out a policy on primary residency for dependents in multi-custodial households, a real edge case that affects local families. Thursday, Planning and Zoning takes on the Carhenge Redevelopment and other Town-owned projects in a dense land-use session.

notable.stake: Second reading vote on wildfire code changes to Land Use Code landscaping and historic review.
New policy on primary residency for dependents in split-custody households could affect housing eligibility.
P&Z reviews subdivision and concept plans for major Town-owned redevelopment at Carhenge site.
